extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, students, and clinicians planning or registering systematic or scoping review protocols (health and social care disciplines)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and registering protocols that describe the rationale, hypotheses, and planned methods for systematic and scoping reviews, and for using protocol registries (e.g., PROSPERO, OSF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare protocol before starting review; make public and register
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic review protocol should be prepared before a review is started and used as a guide to carry out the review. Detailed protocols should be made publicly and registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA (2021) guidance: register protocols to provide a permanent record and to enable comparison of reported review findings with what was planned in the protocol. Registration falls into the first step: Initiate Your Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State the rationale for the review and the specific objectives or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explanation of why the review is needed and the review's aims; listed as a typical protocol item and referenced in PRISMA protocol checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify inclusion and exclusion criteria for studies to be considered in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define populations, interventions/exposures, comparators, outcomes, study designs, settings, timeframes, and any other filters used to determine study eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sources
rubrics_metrics.description: List the databases, registers, websites, and other sources that will be searched for relevant studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe coverage (dates, language restrictions), supplementary sources (trial registers, grey literature), and planned handsearching or contact with authors as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft of a search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a draft search strategy for at least one database (search strings and limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enough detail that the search can be reproduced; a draft search should be included in the protocol (PRISMA recommends this).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how records, data, and files will be managed during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover software/tools for citation management and screening, procedures for deduplication, data storage, and version control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the outcomes of interest and how they will be prioritized for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define primary and secondary outcomes, measurement timepoints, and any methods for prioritizing outcomes when multiple are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the planned methods for synthesizing the extracted data, both quantitative and qualitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether meta-analysis will be performed, planned statistical models, methods for assessing heterogeneity, subgroup or sensitivity analyses, and narrative synthesis approaches if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the PRISMA protocol checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to PRISMA protocol checklist for a complete list of items to include in a systematic review protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists typical items and points readers to the PRISMA protocol checklist for full requirements and reporting exemplars (PRISMA 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: comprehensive introductory elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For scoping review protocols, include an introduction detailing definitions, overall objective, explanation of need, eligibility criteria, and the preliminary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow JBI Reviewer's Manual (chapter 11.2) for specifics; the introduction should set scope and rationale clearly for scoping reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: sample search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a sample literature search strategy for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include draft search strings and primary databases to ensure reproducibility and transparency; JBI and PRISMA-ScR recommend including this in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: explanation of the search report
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the search results and search process will be reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how search dates, number of records retrieved, database-specific strategies, and any limits will be documented in the final report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: study selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the process for selecting studies (screening and eligibility) for scoping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify number of reviewers, screening steps (title/abstract, full-text), conflict resolution procedures, and use of screening tools or software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: draft charting table/data extraction and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a draft charting table or data extraction form and explain planned data items and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List data fields to be extracted, pilot testing plans for the charting form, and procedures for managing missing or unclear data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping review: presentation of results and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how results and extracted data will be presented in the scoping review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State planned tables, charts, mapping approaches, and narrative descriptions to summarize the extent, range, and nature of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register protocols in appropriate registries (PROSPERO, OSF, JBI, Cochrane, Campbell)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use established registries to record key features of the review protocol and maintain a permanent public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO records key features and maintains a permanent record to enable comparison between planned and reported methods; OSF can host files and recommends using the Preregistration or Systematic Review templates; note that some services (JBI) may be subscription-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose registry/template suited to review type and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Select an appropriate registry or platform and template based on review type (systematic vs scoping) and availability (subscription vs open).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO is for health and social care systematic reviews; JBI and Cochrane resources are available but may require subscriptions; OSF is an open platform with recommended templates for preregistration.
